prior_importants.description: The conductor now launches whenever `pup status` says a launch would be allowed. But `pup status` prints `Launch: allowed` while the memory floor or the plan's usage hold would still refuse the launch. The kickoff also says `pup status` shows each limit, including the 1.5 GB floor, which it never prints.

findings.description: With about 1.45 GB up to just under 1.5 GB of memory available, `pup status` prints `Launch: refused (under 1.5 GB of memory available)` beside `memory: 1.5 GB available, 1.5 GB a launch needs`. This happens because `gigabytes()` rounds with toFixed(1). Round down (e.g. `Math.floor(bytes / 1024 ** 3 * 10) / 10`) or print two decimals so the line agrees with the verdict.

When only the usage hold refuses, the verdict reads `only the operator's --over-limit the usage hold`, a clause with no verb. Say `--over-limit lifts the usage hold` so it reads correctly on its own and after the `--over-cap` clause. The pinned strings in session-cap.test.ts and index.test.ts need the same change.

`capOver` repeats the backlog and load comparisons the `over` list already makes, so the `--over-cap` clause can drift from the reasons listed. Compute `backlogOver` and `loadOver` once, use them in `over`, and set `capOver = backlogOver || loadOver`.
No caller passes `launchHolds`'s `now` parameter: the CLI and both tests call it with the repo path alone. Drop the parameter and pass `Date.now()` to `assertUsageRoom` inside.
The new booleans `usageHeld`, `capOver` and `lowMemory` don't start with is/has/should/can, as general.md §Type safety requires. Rename them, e.g. `isUsageHeld`, `isCapOver`, `isMemoryLow`.
